content:
Manchester United moved swiftly on Friday evening to secure the arrival of Manuel Ugarte from Paris Saint-Germain, agreeing a deal worth €50m (£42m) with a further €10m tied to bonuses. By nightfall the paperwork was complete, and the 23-year-old had committed his future to a five-year agreement, with an option that could extend his stay by another 12 months.

Those close to the negotiations described a transfer driven by clarity: United wanted a specialist ball-winner in the middle, a player comfortable doing the difficult, unglamorous work that allows others to flourish. For Erik ten Hag, it marked a major step in shaping a squad that can control matches with greater authority. Ugarte’s arrival also gives the manager a second senior holding midfielder alongside Casemiro, increasing both competition and resilience across a long season.

In his first words after signing, Ugarte struck an unapologetically ambitious tone. He spoke of joining “a club of this magnitude,” of being drawn in by the plan presented to him, and of a determination to give everything for those around him. It was not just a statement of intent, but a promise of attitude: sacrifice, collective commitment, and a fixation on silverware. He made clear he feels a responsibility to help lift the club back toward the standards that its supporters expect, and he referenced the pull of Old Trafford as something he has long wanted to experience for himself.

United’s new sporting director, Dan Ashworth, underlined that the recruitment team saw Ugarte as one of the key priorities of the summer. Behind the scenes, the club’s leadership framed the deal as part of a broader rebuild—one focused on players entering their prime, with the mentality to handle pressure and the hunger to drive standards daily.

For Ugarte, the challenge begins immediately: adapting to the pace and scrutiny that follow United everywhere, earning trust in a demanding role, and translating words into performances that raise the level of those around him. For the club, the signing is another signal that the rebuild is being pushed with purpose—one more piece intended to turn optimism into tangible progress.

Any other questions?.
